title: Resource Embargo vs. Tier 1 Survival (Hawkins-Simon Viability)
question: What happens to basic survival if outside suppliers cut the commons off?
target_article: Article 3.1 — Thermodynamic Boundary & Article 3.5 — Strategic Physical Reserves
scenario: A hostile legacy jurisdiction cuts 30–80% of the external inputs a bioregion imports. Does the input-output economy still deliver Tier 1 survival, and do the reserves bridge the gap?
exploit_summary: A reproducible SIMONE run showed that the old proof standard (non-negative Leontief output) can never fail, so it proved nothing. The matrix had no import or capacity data, so embargo resilience could not even be measured, and grain-only reserves did not cover heat, water and fresh produce.
constitutional_countermeasure: New Article 3.1.6 (Tier 1 Autarkic Closure) requires an annual public audit proving that every sector directly or indirectly supplying Tier 1 needs, including shelter and healthcare, can meet full Tier 1 demand from local resources and installed capacity alone, with external inputs at zero and a published reserve margin. Article 3.5.2 now composes reserves according to the audit gaps: storable stocks, spare parts, and redundant productive capacity for goods that cannot be stored. Evidence: simone/benchmarks/sim_qa_10_embargo.jl.
verdict_human: RED TEAM WON — constitution patched: survival must be proven autarkic every year

human_summary.lead: The attack exposed a real gap, so we changed the Constitution instead of explaining it away.
points: The old test could never fail, so it proved nothing about embargoes.
Each bioregion must now show, every year, that it can feed, heat, house and heal everyone with zero imports.
Reserves are planned around the measured gaps, including spare machines for things you cannot store, such as heat.

title: Petition Flooding & Sortition Jury Exhaustion
question: Can a faction paralyze a sortition council by flooding it with petitions?
target_article: Article 4.3 — Stratified Selection, Universal Service, and Anti-Bureaucratic Rotation
scenario: A coordinated faction floods a 15-citizen council with bad-faith petitions until jurors burn out and good-faith requests expire.
exploit_summary: The constitution had no petition-intake procedure. In a synthetic model, a 5% faction cut the share of good-faith petitions heard within 8 weeks from 99.7% to 2.0%, and jurors worked more than 15 hours per week all year.
constitutional_countermeasure: New Article 4.3.5: publication is never filtered, but agenda placement requires co-endorsement by a fixed share of constituents. Everyone holds an equal endorsement allowance, never conditioned on labor, conduct or opinion. Agenda slots are finite and filled by public lottery weighted by distinct support, and a rotating 3-citizen Triage Panel checks form and merges duplicates without ever judging merit. Burnout disappeared in every simulated run, but a fully mobilized 20% faction can still claim about half of agenda slots, so the verdict remains provisional pending calibration. Evidence: simone/benchmarks/sim_qa_11_petition_dos.py.
verdict_human: RED TEAM WON — patched; residual risk openly documented

human_summary.lead: Anyone can still publish anything, but getting onto the agenda now takes real, equal, non-buyable support.
points: Each person gets the same small endorsement budget, and spending it on many petitions gets quadratically expensive.
Agenda slots are limited and drawn by public lottery, so volume alone cannot capture the council.
The fix is not perfect: a large organized group still gets a share of agenda time roughly proportional to its size.

title: Internal Contradictions Audit (Weapons, Thresholds, Labor Sanctions, Review)
question: Does the Constitution contradict itself anywhere?
scenario: A critic quotes the Constitution against itself: a weapons ban next to autonomous strike platforms, a 66% threshold outside the 75/60/50 ladder, a single-citizen veto, labor sanctions that strip voting rights, and no body empowered to declare acts void.
exploit_summary: All contradictions were real and verifiable by quotation. Worst case: a faction controlling work rosters could assign dissidents impossible shifts and legally strip their sortition rights.
constitutional_countermeasure: Interception is limited to uncrewed machines and never targets persons, and standoff action is limited to non-lethal disablement (Arts. 7.1.2, 8.1.3, 8.1.4). The 66% threshold is replaced by the standard ladder (Art. 10.5.3). A threshold arithmetic rule is added (Art. 4.5.4), and the single-citizen veto becomes an appealable certification (Art. 2.6.2). The suspension of sortition rights is WITHDRAWN: political rights are never conditioned on labor, and Tier 1 shelter is never conditioned (Art. 5.2). A Constitutional Review Jury of 101 citizens drawn by lot is created (Art. 4.6). Freedom of association is reconciled with the ban on delegate capture (Art. 4.1.3), and supermajorities may expand but never diminish Chapter I rights (Arts. 4.5.1, 8.6.2).
verdict_human: RED TEAM WON — one provision withdrawn, eight articles corrected

human_summary.lead: When the critics are right, the text changes. Your vote can no longer be taken away for missing work shifts.
points: Defense machines may only stop incoming machines, never people.
All voting thresholds now follow one consistent ladder with explicit arithmetic.
A citizen jury drawn by lot now decides whether any law or decree violates the Constitution.

title: Technology Lock-In: Engineering Details Frozen in the Constitution
question: Why does the Constitution no longer name specific technologies?
scenario: Specific battery chemistries, radio brands, timers and weapon types written into the Constitution, some of them in the unamendable Chapter I, would legally freeze better future technology out of the commons.
exploit_summary: Engineering parameters protected by a 75% supermajority, or by absolute entrenchment in Chapter I, create obsolescence lock-in and give critics easy factual targets, such as unverified safety claims.
constitutional_countermeasure: The Constitution now states only functional requirements. Technologies and parameters move to the Organic Law Annex (OL-1 to OL-9), which is amendable by a 60% qualified majority under a ratchet rule (it may never weaken a constitutional guarantee) and reviewable under Article 4.6 (anchored by Art. 10.6.4). Unverified quantitative claims are labelled PROVISIONAL — UNVERIFIED.
verdict_human: RED TEAM WON — technology moved to an amendable Organic Law Annex

human_summary.lead: The Constitution says what must be guaranteed; a separate, easier-to-update annex says which technology does it today.
points: Better technology can be adopted without a constitutional amendment.
No technical rule can ever lower a constitutional protection.
Unproven numbers are openly marked as provisional.
